metadata.school_name: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

analysis.name: Andrew Pease
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took MATH 130 with him. He is a cool and stylish person, but not a good teacher at all. He deserves to be teaching higher level maths and not pre-calc because he overcomplicates simple concepts making it very hard to follow along. I strongly advise not taking this class with him if you are taking a lot of other STEM courses.

10/10 would not recommend. TAs were SO unhelpful and the professor overcomplicates simple topics. I definitely could have done better but l think the way he teaches is directed for higher level math and not pre-calc. He is a very stylistic and funny person and very accessible outside of class with his office hours.

I took math 130 with professor pease, it was terrible. The class itself is not too hard, but the way he explained concepts got very confusing very fast. You have to spend a lot of time outside of class learning the concepts before you can get to actually studying them.
Nice guy who seems like he's trying his best, but the whole class is confused and not doing as well as they should on the exams. I have a tutor and learn from YouTube better than he explains it.

Professor Pease made math 130 much harder than it should've been. The class is graded majority from midterms and the finals. I recommend not taking this class with a heavy course load and getting a tutor asap.

take_again_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably worse than older ones.

analysis.name: Lorna Avilés
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Aviles is hands down the best professor I have had at UNC so far. Although speaking in a different language can be daunting, she encourages practice and genuinely cares about whether or not you are learning. Participation matters to stay engaged, but class would fly by, as she's a great teacher and not a boring lecturer. TAKE HER CLASS!!!

Professor Aviles is amazing. Her lectures are interesting and engaging and she doesn't take herself too seriously. Her course load is made to challenge you and help you succeed (if you put in the work). She returns graded work so so fast. Seriously, she is the kind of professor that makes you happy you paid for college. Take her class.

Don't let other reviews fool you, this is NOT an easy A class. There are a handful of grammar quizzes throughout the semester that can tank your grade, the in-class essays that can be graded somewhat tough in terms of grammar, and the examsare fairly graded, but you have to study and be familar with the content.

One of the best Spanish professors that I have had at UNC so far! She is encouraging, a fair grader, and wants every student to succeed. The class projects are also very fun and engaging to learn about businesses across Latin America.

I took prof Avilés for span 344 and loved it! You will spend a lot of class time discussing readings, the lesson, etc with peers and I feel it really improved my speaking skills in a chill environment. The papers aren't hard and you can often take them in your own direction to keep it fresh. There is a group presentation but it isn't hard. Take it!

analysis.name: Arthur Eddy
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His teaching style was often disorganized and course expectations/grading criteria weren't communicated clearly. Assignments required a significant amount of work, sometimes without sufficient guidance or clarification. Lots of guest speakers. Overall, the instructor did not seem very flexible or understanding when students raised concerns.

Prof Eddy was great, very accessible, and helpful with questions. There is no rubric for any assignments, which made it sometimes difficult to understand feedback and grades. The class is boring because its a prereq, but Prof Eddy did provide good advice about the real world and had educational guest lectures.

I learned a great deal in Prof Eddy's class. He cared for all his students. There is a ton of group project which makes class fun. There were a few guest speakers from different industries that added to the class. I highly recommend his class.

I don't go here, because I'm in high school, but this guy is my godfather and I would like to mention that. He's pretty good at being a godfather, I think, but please don't let him wear suits. Otherwise someone might mistake him for Jeff Bezos and that would be bad.

This class was a bit different from my other classes, but in a good way. His class is combo of lectures, group projects and guests to speak to the class along with the main project. I learned a lot from his class.

analysis.name: Fenaba Addo
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was extremely repetitive with the same content in every single module. Prof. Addo does NOT know how to lecture in any way shape or form. She needs to take a workshop on lecturing. The class itself was boring, tests were fine, just study the review that she posts. Application based. Our assignments were easy 100's. I skipped class a lot.

I found her class frustrating. She is condescending and fails to answer questions beyond the content of her lecture slides. The content is manageable, but lectures are poorly organized. My biggest issue with her class was the volume of tests. A policy innovation and analysis course should focus on research and writing, not multiple choice exams.

She is clearly smart but such a bad lecturer. She gets confused by her own slides, mostly just reads off them anyway, and struggles to answer student questions. She also weirdly giggles so much and it makes me so angry. Exams weren't too hard though and out of class assignments were easy 100s

Professor Addo cares a lot and is knowledgable but her lectures were verbatim off the slides. She was not great at answering student questions in lecture either. 4 exams throughout the semester which was a lot but if you study the guide she gives then you should do well on them. Easy class and interesting content but unhelpful lectures.

Very nice person and is willing to help you outside of class, but isn't always good at answering questions. We had three midterm exams and one final exam with 5 policy assignments throughout the semester, which felt like a lot, but if you study the lecture content well you're fine. She reads straight off the slides which isn't helpful.

analysis.name: Ashley Anderson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 123 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Great class and professor overall, but didn't love the communication between professor and I. She's very nice but unavailable. I showed up to her office hours once, waited an hour and a half just to find out that she was in Europe and didn't notify her students. This was a week before finals. But everything other than that about the class was fine.

Professor Anderson is disgustingly and dangerously educated. She makes lectures engaging and is very knowledgeable in pretty much everything she talks about. Attendance is required. There's weekly quizzes with five questions and two papers, along with the midterm and final that make up your grade. She challenges you, but an A is possible!

This class definitely felt a little harder for a 100-level course, compared to the other poli-sci courses i've taken here. Weekly quizzes were lowkey annoying, and readings were so long, but the class was okay and the lectures were good. Also hateeeee the fact that the exams are weighed 30% mcq and 70% essay, like dude, this is so ta biased.

I took POLI 130 with her, and she was pretty great! Informative lectures, clearly knows her subject matter, and encourages class participation. Readings are the main homework, and are necessary to know for the midterm and final. Additionally, I would recommend checking the lecture handouts for the key terms, because those will also be on the tests.

Super interesting lecture and class material. Anderson is incredibly knowledgeable. None of the assignments are very difficult; however, almost impossible to get an A, given 80% of your grade comes from just 4 assignments (2 papers and a written midterm and final / have to really crush the papers) + extra credit assignments were really dumb imo.

take_again_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably better than older ones.

analysis.name: Jon Abramowitz
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Abramowitz was always funny during lectures. Always willing to help. You're graded on 2 midterms, a final, and a few case studies (group assignment). No grade cushioning, but exams are pretty straightforward, mostly factual and not application based. Attendance is not graded but you have to come to class since he puts very little on his slides.

Super chill professor. Nice, friendly, easily accessible. Willing to give feedback. Good lectures. Expects participation (part of your grade). Interesting lectures. Would definitely take this professor again.

Seriously the best prof I've ever taken at UNC. He's very passionate about the material and his tests reflect the lectures well. The only "complaint" I have is that he doesn't post his full ppts online, so you have to go to class to get all the info. 75% of the grade is tests & 25% final essay, so take that for what you will. 10/10 would take again

TAKE THIS CLASS: super interesting and great lectures. Some topics were more interesting than others but Abramowitz always made them enjoyable. He is a really cool guy and great teacher. The grade is based on 3 exams and 2 papers. The exams are fair if you take good notes. You can't miss any class though because he doesn't post the full slideshows.

Professor Abramowitz is a super fun and interesting lecturer. I love that he helps illustrate concepts using stories from his own experience as a clinical psychologist. The class is very easy - the tests only have questions from the lectures, so reading the textbook is completely unneccesary. Besides the three tests, there is just one final paper.

good_rating_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably worse than older ones.

analysis.name: Allison Schlobohm
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Schlobohm is awesome, she is incredible caring and passionate. You do have to do work in this class, but its school so thats normal. It's never overbearing but it is work and thats okay. Overall she is awesome, and I would recommend taking her class.

Dr. Schlobohm was a charming professor and emphasized that her class was more about experimentation than getting things right. The class structure is centered around "if you put the work in, you'll get an A," which is a fantastic change of pace from traditional lectures, especially about personal branding. Plus, she loves feedback for the class!

Dr. Schlobohm is an incredible professor. She makes writing and oral presentation material engaging and interesting and is receptive to feedback, even if critical. The classroom culture is kind and safe. Though she is a hard grader, her feedback is thorough and applicable. I can attest to the growth in hard and soft skills I've had because of her.

Professor Schlobohm cares about her students, but has a strict attendance policy and takes a very long time to return feedback. Her grading scale is also very difficult, and considers a B in her class to be "very good". While she works to make classes engaging, it's hard to do well and gives only 1-2 students per class above 90 on each assignment.

Dr. Schlobohm's personality wasn't for me, but her class was fine. She's nice enough, cares about the content, and the work isn't hard because its very self-oriented, but she takes forever to grade and her scores seemed unfair. For our final presentation, the highest score she gave was a 90. Deceptively easy class.

analysis.name: Andy Bechtel
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bechtel provided many opportunities to ask for help or suggestions while completing assignments, plus plenty of good feedback once they were complete. I would absolutely take another class with him as he very obviously truly cares about the students and wants to help prepare them for their future careers.

All but one assignment is done in class, and they're all very straightforward. A few group assignments here and there. A great class for all journalists. Andy is kind, direct and knowledgable, and he cares about his students. One of my all-time favorite j-school professors!

Andy Bechtel made this class incredible. He cared so much and is such a wonderful guy. He gave amazing feedback on assignments and ample time to complete all assignments. Taught all of the content very well. This class was not stressful for me but I learned a lot. I am a better writer after taking his class. 20/10 recommend him!!

Prof. Bechtel makes this class quite easy. He grades the assignments generously and leaves great feedback. The exams are not very stressful and are a small part of the grade compared to the assignments. This class definitely made me a better writer with minimal stress. Would highly recommend.

This was a really good class. Clear expectations, quick and thorough feedback, and Andy's just a genuinely nice guy. He's super passionate about the material. It was a long class but we never had homework. If you like editing/grammar, this will be an easy class, and probably really enjoyable, too. You'll be a better news editor afterwards.

analysis.name: Agnieszka Majewska
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is super sweet and the class itself is not hard if you pay attention. No textbook or anything like that and the homework she assigns takes like 5 minutes. I love her she's the best
Super sweet professor and really cares about teaching the polish language. Even though it's a quite difficult language, she made it much easier and so much fun!
Prof Majewska is so kind and genuine. She prepares us well for exams and announces what topics will be on each quiz/test beforehand. It is not difficult to get an A in this class.

Professor Majewska is a very sweet and authentic Polish Professor. She gives a daily completion homework, the occasional graded homework, four quizzes, two tests and a final presentation. Everything is super easy and requires mild-to-moderate effort. Everything is easily outlined, and her lessons are easy to follow. I am\ taking 402 and 403.

Majewska is an absolute gem. I went in with 0 Polish knowledge and ended up having her for 3 semesters. She is very understanding and is as helpful as she can be. The key to her class is quizlets and repetition. There are plenty of opportunities for grades and the final exam is a low percentage of the grade.

good_rating_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably worse than older ones.

analysis.name: Emily Burkhead
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 251 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The class itself is not horrible, you can preview by looking up "understanding analysis" and practice. Tests decide your grade, not hard if you know how to apply a theorem or prove it. She hates to grade higher for those who improved, and she grades harsh, bonus and curve are almost nothing, I regret taking her hunger game class only for a minor.

Taking Calculus 3 with this professor was the worst experience of my life. Studying for her exams brought me to tears. The test study guides are an extremely poor representation of the exams and she wrote most of the final so her students did bad on that too. Her class average is a C, while others are an A. Do not take this class! Save your GPA!!!

I gave her a 4/5 when I took her for MATH233. That was a lie. Tests and homework were graded harshly which would have been fine if she curved generously. Given what she said is "on track for an A/B/C" after each midterm, the curve should have been like +13% when it was actually +3%. Ragebait incarnate.

Carefully assess your abilities. There's no curve for this class at all. It's the only one among 233 courses that requires a weekly exam. Also, I've seen exams from other sections that had only five simple questions in 50 minutes, but Professor Burkhead's test contained more than 20 challenging and time-consuming problems, with no extra time given.

Save your grade and don't take 381 with Burkhead. Inaccessible and hard to approach with questions related to grading or asking her to explain concepts. Asked her many times to explain the material, and was often met with snarky remarks. Office hours are even worse, as she is not much help if you're lost.

analysis.name: Teressa Bergland
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 101 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: As others have said, her exams are quite long.  However, she has recognized that the exams weren't completely fair and offered revisions worth half credit back.  Her lectures are pretty good and she's very accessible via office hours.  Homework is pretty light.  She's not perfect but def way better than some  of the other stor profs here.

these reviews are way too harsh... there are professors genuinely so much worse than her, and they still have a better rating. it seemed like she struggled a lot with anxiety and felt disorganized often times, but she was passionate and tried her best. her exams were very hard, as the other comments suggest, but it was not anything impossible.

Rated her 2 (not 1) bc she does genuinely have a passion and it shows in her good lectures. HOWEVER, she is not meant to be a professor. Harsh/rigid grading and closed-note tests aren't sensible for a coding class, and tests (that she made) not graded for 1-2 months. She tries to do too much then penalizes the students when she finds out she can't.

SHE IS A GOOD TEACHER. People need to chill on her because she is genuinely good at her job, but she teaches a hard class so people are bound to get bad grades. She does her best, and while it takes her a long time to grade, she is very generous with extra credit. You are going to struggle in this class if you dont like STATS, but she does her best

I do not understand other reviews. Is she the best professor? No, but she's a fine one. It's clear that she's adjusting to teaching here, but, her exams were quite fair. You'll struggle if you don't show up to class/study, but you'll do fine if you pay attention. Not an easy A, but you'll get a good grade if you show up and put in a little effort.

analysis.name: Alaina Garland
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 423 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Unless you want to learn random facts, such as the length of fruit fly's stuff or the debates around religion and evolution, do not take this course. Dr. Garland chooses to spend time on minor details that do not appear on the test, and thus does not effectively teach the class. Do not take BIO 101 with Dr. Garland. Save yourself the trouble.

I've never made one of these so you the fact that I had to take time to make this should be a warning. She has NO business teaching at the undergraduate level. If she taught Intro to ABCs I would not take it with her. I've had elementary teachers that are more capable of teaching than her. She is by far the WORST professor I have ever come across.

For starters, I hate this class. I took AP and honors Bio in high school and got As and then get a 36 on the first test. I would study for hours and the questions on the test did not make any sense what so ever. STAY CLEAR if you do not want to tank your GPA. She wastes time making a seating chart for a 400 person class instead of teaching.

Dr. Garland is such a sweetheart but you should steer clear of this course. The exams are harder than the material is to understand. And the lectures are fluffy and unhelpful. I'm hoping to be premed and this course made me genuinely reconsider whether I was fit for it. Do yourself a favor and take any other Professor. It's not worth the trouble.

Dr. Garland wastes a lot of lecture time going over useless information including but not limited to preaching about career goals. Tests are very tricky and seem to test test taking ability more rather than knowledge. Lecture lowkey useless, but she's definitely caring. Just not a great prof. Get ready to study and read the textbook.

analysis.name: Brett Whalen
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 88 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Whalen is a great professor who LOVES what he does and is always happy to give feedback on essays. The class was very interesting and discussion based, but NOT an easy A seminar. We watched a movie and read documents weekly outside of class. Part of your grade is from participation in discussions/group presentations and essays.

So many old, boring movies. Watched about 10 films, no color, silent, 3 hours long, and some in other languages, and most were not great. Had to read a chapter a week that barely related to move. There is a big group project, so hope for good group. MUST PARTICIPATE.

Genuinely the best professor I've had here. He was very passionate about the material.  Short readings and watching films.  If you don't like participating in class discussions, this class isn't for you.  Take a class with him if you have the chance.
Dr. Whalen is obviously incredibly passionate about the Medieval period and his students. Interacting with him is an excellent way to improve the uniqueness of his class.

Dr. Whalen is a great professor. He really knows his stuff and is very excited to be teaching it. He structures the class so it does not burden you too much. However, the assignments do not have clear grading criteria. Overall, a great class though and I would definitely recommend.

analysis.name: Michael Beeler
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is a great guy who cares about his students and keeps class interesting and engaging, one of my favorite teachers in the B school. Wouldn't take anyone else for 403.

This class is fine if you are not (ad-libs). I honestly had a hard time with the content and the structure of the course so figure out a way to study/be able to structure yourself to take the exam in class. There are a lot of resources and examples, he has a lot of knowledeg!! dont be afraid to ask

Honestly the best class i've taken at KF. What a lad. Made me excited to come to class every day and spent the first 20 mins of class just yapping and telling jokes. Content for me was extremely enjoyable and all the exams are open note so extremely easy to do good on. Group project however is slightly annoying if u have incompetent group members.

Oh Beeler where do I even begin. Ever since I met u on our first day I knew I was in for a great sem. Had me jumping for joy to come to class every day and put a smile on my face every time I saw u (shi I think i'm in love). I came in expecting spreadsheets and pain and I left with memories, laughs and a disturbing level of emotional attachment

Professor Beeler was by far the best teacher I've ever had. We spent the first 20 min of every class telling jokes, something good, etc before going into lecture which made learning and the class enviornment really enjoyable. He gives you literally every resource you need to succeed in the class and  made me lmao every day.

analysis.name: Emily Baragwanath
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is an amazing lecturer, but most of the grading is from the TAs; they are really sweet too though. You def need to do your readings to be up to date with the class and prepared, and there are a good bit of written assignments, but as long as you read and listen you will be perfectly fine
Not difficult but not interesting.  Don't take unless you're passionate about greek history.  Lots of reading expected for a gen-ed.  Not graded harshly, but only a few things were graded.

Emily is... amazing, to say the least. She specializes in historiography, so you will come out of the course knowing more about Greek historians and the practice of writing history in the ancient world than you ever would have expected. As far as the material itself, it is difficult Greek, but Dr. Baragwanath knows what she is doing and helps you.

Prof. Baragwanath is very knowledgeable and passionate about the course. Decent amount of reading and writing, but as long as you pay attention and stay on top of the readings you'll be fine. Really enjoyed this course.

Prof. B truly was amazing. She is extremely passionate about the classics and she is so personable that I would invite her to my wedding. The course is extremely reading heavy so my only setbacks in the class were if I did not do all of the readings. If you engage, you will do well. Assignments are given in the syllabus so no surprises.

analysis.name: Tonya Balan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Balan is good at making things make sense, especially if you have no expereince in computer/data science. Her class is very easy but it is just her lecturing, labs on friday are when you  get to actually interact with class material and the people in your class. Final is a group project, but watch out for quiz 2 it is harder than quiz 1.

Balan is very fair and she makes class super welcoming for beginners to Python and Stats. Attendance is mandatory but counted only on days where there's classwork, so many skip if they know the material. Two exams which are super easy and similar to study guides. Lab session about once every 2 weeks where you work on a very simple group project.

Prof. Balan is an extremely kind woman and teaches a great data110 class. She formats it so you can learn a ton about coding if you want to, but doesn't make your grade dependent on being really good at data science. She lets you use notecards for the 2 exams. Final group project. Definitely take this class if you need a stats credit.

Professor Balan was awesome. There are 2 quizzes and a final group video project. A couple things do get a little technical with some code and using the correct formulas, but if you study, you will be fine. Attendance is optional but she brought several guest speakers who were interesting to hear, so I'd suggest going. Very good experience.

Super chill and knowledgable professor. Final project was fun and just enough of a challenge. Gemini makes all labs and homework a cakewalk. Quizzes are clearly laid out beforehand with ample review material. Incredibly easy class and material is taught if you actually want to learn it. Take if you need a stats credit but don't want to learn stats.

analysis.name: David Baker
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the most intelligent professors I have had. Honestly, the class is slightly disorganized. No clear grading criteria (check plus check check minus), no clear grades included in the syllabus. Had to read a play every 5 classes, so lots of reading, but the discussions were insanely intelligent and I learned so so much.

I loved this class! Shakespeare felt very daunting previously, but Professor Baker's discussion-led classes provide ample opportunities for questions. He is very passionate about the subject and although he teaches based on his theories for each play, he is very open to feedback and every single classmate's interpretations.

Not the worst class, but it was more thanks to Shakespeare being a cool subject than Baker himself. Its fine, but I was definitely tempted to skip more often than the maximum 2 classes. He more argues his opinions on the works than teaches... points if you can argue intelligently with him though!
Lecture heavy, but lectures are interesting and he relates everything in a way you can understand it. Very funny and understanding about things that come up. He makes dry material interesting!

You read a Shakespeare play on your own, and you'll discuss a particular play for 2-3 class periods. I was personally never exposed to Shakespeare before this class, and I found it both interesting and doable. I recommend taking this class even if you're the slightest bit curious.

review_highlights.comment: 3 midterms, fairly easy if you pay attention and take good notes in class. Final was not bad but definitely more challenging than the midterms but if you really lock in an A is 100% possible. Not a ton of HW, only critique is sometimes he isn't super clear explaining things so if math doesn't come easy to you it may be hard to grasp.

Chill guy, good lectures, and very straightforward class if you pay attention. Final was comparably harder than midterms but nothing impossible. Only con is that he takes off points for punctual mistakes and not answering a question the way he wants to.
He is a very very nice person. However, I don't think he is a very good instructor. It can be very difficult to understand difficult topics with him as an instructor. There are better options.

I had Corbin for Math 152. He's a nice guy and does a good job explaining new concepts. His exams don't prepare you for the final which is much harder than anything you learn in class. My grade went from an A- to a B because of the final.

He's a chill dude and his exams are easy, but I wouldn't recommend taking his class. Corbin is not a great professor and doesn't answer questions well. He does not prepare you for the final; I went from an A- to a C+.

analysis.name: Esther Campi
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If you think you hate PR, I would HIGHLY RECOMMEND taking this class! Professor Campi makes the content so enjoyable that you'd probably find yourself reading the textbook in your free time. She's also such a cool person with very cool experiences under her belt. I think we were allowed 5 absences but I never took any because it was that fun.
The comments speak for themselves. I wish she taught more classes so I could take her again. Possibly the best professor at UNC she's so awesome you won't regret taking her classes!

While Professor Campi's capabilities within the classroom are heavily reflected in her perfect rating, there is no rating that can encapsulate the quality of person she is on a daily basis. She is by far and away my favorite professor I have had at UNC, and is someone that I admire in every way I know how. I could not recommend her enough. 10/10

One of the best professors I have had. If you get the chance definitely take a class with her. I usually don't like talking in class, and Prof. Campi made me want to. This class is super interesting and she gives a lot of real-world advice so it's super applicable!

The comments speak for themselves so I am not really doing anyone a service by writing another. However, in case she reads these, I want Professor Campi to know that she greatly impacts each of her students in a wonderful way. I aspire to be more like her as a person and will always remember her 10 last bits of advice.

analysis.name: Christopher Handy
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 175 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I'm not sure if it was because i've never taken any type of statistics class before, but I did not follow a single thing he said. unclear guest lectures. exams questions not released for review. course flow doesn't make sense. homework doesn't impact class grade. often quizzed before lecture on the topic. bar for an a is too high (94). overall her lectures were unclear. difficult to anticipate exam qs. she is somewhat nice but i wish she would've cared more.

analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She was an amazing teacher. You learn a lot of things in this class that are useful in the professional world (memos, letters, cover letters, resumes, research proposals, etc.) I would suggest taking this class even if you aren't interested in business. She is a tough grader but gives you a lot of help. She is incredibly friendly.
Prof. Irons is such a good professor! Conversation in the classroom was always well-guided by her and captivating in general!

Irons is great to improve your writing. REALLY though grader tho. Sometimes she'd take off points and no one would know why. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS WITH YOUR ROUGH DRAFTSshe will tell you what to fix & your grade will be much higher! Real-world consulting group projects are a huge part of the class. Very interesting & no experience necessary

She is a sweet lady. There is a colossal amount of reading (5 novels plus countless short stories).  Just skim the bad ones (most) and contribute to discussion. There is a 8-10 p. analytical paper worth 25% of your grade, final exam 25%, midterm 20%, biweekly 1-2 page text responses 20%, and attend/partic 10%. Too many texts, too little depth. 4/5.

This class really should be a 4 credit hour class, not 3. There is so much outside work, the grading rubrics are unclear, and even after going to office hours and taking Dr. Irons' feedback to heart in my revisions on assignments, my grades still stay around the same range. Dr Irons cares about her students, but if you take this, get ready to work

analysis.name: Jordynn Jack
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: My queen. Dr. Jack is an incredible scholar and absolutely lovely to have as a professor. She's exceptionally smart, but she's not at all intimidating -- she's a very warm, flexible instructor, and you'll learn a lot in her classes. All hail. Highly recommend taking courses with her, even if you're not an English major.

Dr. Jack was very personable and made a clear effort to know everyone's names, even if you weren't an avid participant. The course material was a bit boring at times, but Dr. Jack worked hard to make it interactive and hands-on as often as possible.

Such a lovely individual. This class was very relaxing and reminded me of the close-knit and collaborative environment I miss so dearly in high school. The work is very easy and minimal. I made some of my close friends from this class, too, and picked up some new hobbies (we got to cross stitch, play with typewriters, and more!) Very fun :)

This is a straight forward class, but don't expect any knowledge to be spoon-fed to you. This class emphasizes  working at your own pace, so much of what you take away depends on you. It's useful in forcing you to create a finished, professional product. Dr. Jack was very accommodating and insightful- all qualities you could want from a professor.

Dr. Jack is the best professor I have had thus far. Her lectures are relevant, and I know I will use a lot of the skills she taught in class beyond my undergraduate career. She gives helpful feedback on every assignment, and her time management is impeccable. If you get the chance to take a class with her, 100% do it. She also teaches ENGL 300I!

analysis.name: Ivonne Chirino-Klevans
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: literally 0 feedback on anything in a timely manner. also her quiz questions are very poorly framed and I don't even think she knows what she's asking on them. Ok professor and knows the material but is kind of just disconnected from the course and picks groups for you so your entire grade can literally hinge on a group at the beginning of the sem

If you read the textbook and study on your own, you should be fine. However, she told us just to study vocab and then only put 3 vocab questions out of 25 on the quiz. Her slides are also very unclear and she doesn't share them. Overall, not very clear or amenable.

Loved the fun interactive activities we did in class; however, she grades kinda harshly with vague instructions. Gave many groups mid 70s-80s on the final group project, which didn't have a rubric. Class quizzes seemed easy, but turned out difficult for no reason. The final was recycled from past quizzes, so that was nice. try to participate

Ivonne is a nice person, but I agree with the review that said you can't disagree with her or she may take it personally. The course doesn't encourage grasping content but more-so just memorizing vocab. Silly in-class activities. Final project instructions were vague and the rubric she used to grade it was never given out.

I first reached out to Dr. Klevans after our first class. I was concerned about comments I had heard about class participation. Don't take this class if you don't like team activities or are kind of shy. I got an A but the hardest was to have to participate in class.

analysis.name: Danielle James
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very kind and encouraging prof, wants everyone to engage in discussions during class. Plenty of advance warning for in-class tests. Manageable amount of reading, never took more than 1-1.5 hours to prep for discussions. Go to office hours!

Prof. James is approachable and kind and gives good lectures. She's open to all perspectives and brings a sense of humor to class. She helped me improve as a writer. The reading load is completely manageable (~25 pages a class).

Professor James is incredibly kind. I honestly learned more than I expected in. I earned an A but this required an EXTREME amount of hours and effort. I would compare this 100 level class to a 300 level course at UNC. Feedback on midterm is only available via office hours and is largely based on the “vibe” of your writing rather than a rubric.

THE HARDEST A I'VE EVER HAD. I'm a dual stem major and this was way too much for a 100-lvl class. I really enjoyed the format and lectures but the workload/grading are par with my 400-lvl core classes. I did every reading (10hrs/wk) and studied 20hrs per exam, and BARELY managed to scrape up an A. Rating isn't lower bc problem is the class not her.

This NEW 100-level entry course only has 4 grades in the class: 2 papers, a midterm, and a final. There are no assignments, activities, slides, or lecture notes. Read 5-6 readings before each class. Her extremely harsh grading is only acceptable for a higher-level required class for SCLL students. I don't recommend this class at all.

Lovely professor, lectures can move pretty fast, but if you pay attention and come to class its no problem. Also the assignments were very reasonable and same with the exams.

review_highlights.comment: I liked Prof Lawton (although idk if she liked me). She starts every class with games and time for us to talk about our weeks. She's also very funny and loves gossip. She did give us maybe 1-3 assignments per week, but I think that's fair for a class that only meets once a week. We also had to write our own plays as a group, which was a lot of fun.

Professor Lawton is the kindest professor I have had at UNC, and she is also so funny and personable. Class is basically just a gossip session with your friends and sharing all your opinions on the reading for the week. It is such an easy A, but also a class that you'll look forward to every week!

Professor Lawton can best be described as angel. She is one of the kindest individuals I have ever met. Her passion for addressing intersectionality through drama comes from a deep seated passion for the topics. This class will force you to think and learn, but will be one of the most inclusive and nurturing environments you will find at unc.

TAKE THIS CLASS! Prof Lawton is AMAZING. She cares so much for her students and her grading policy allows for basically unlimited extra time on assignments and you can still get an A. The assignments are graded for completion and a lot of class time is spent playing games!

Professor Lawton was a fantastic Professor who is passionate about the content she is teaching and is caring. In the course, you read approximately one play each week with about two assignments. would only really take this class if you are a political science major. i took this for the gen-ed credit and had a hard time. lectures are boring, Roberts moves through material super quick, and tests are relatively hard. you def can do well, but it requires A LOT of studying/work.

Dr. J is a very knowledgeable and passionate professor, engaging lectures that are a must attend to be successful. Overall great course, highly recommend Dr. J!

This class was tech free for the first time. It made things a little difficult because she would change stuff based on how we did. In the course we had 3 key term check ins which were essentially our only grades besides the final (which was a timed handwritten essay). I think the course was very manageable and enjoyable. Also depends on your TA.

Genuinely learned so much in this class. Her lectures alone make this class worth taking. The assignments were tedious, but there were only three of them so it was not that bad. If you're interested in history and also need a class that isn't too stressful, take this one! There are also many extra credit opportunities if you're struggling.

She had a no tech policy which almost made me drop the class and I am so glad I did not. Dr.J makes the lectures super interesting and the class often flew by. She ensures you are prepared for the three check-ins throughout the semester, and they are graded generously. Only graded on a few items, 3 check-ins, participation, and final paper.

If an angel had come down from the heavens and you asked me who I thought it was, I would say that Dr. Jeffrey Johnson had arrived. Having him as my Orgo 2 professor has been the most enjoyable class experience I have had at UNC so far. Great energy, a fantastic sense of humor, and an amazing professor.
He was an amazing lecturer and a fun teacher. Would absolutely take again. The difficulty wasn't his fault, it's because it was Orgo II...

Ngl id recommend finding outside study materials, but still Johnson is a pretty solid choice. Lectures are very monotone and old-fashioned on the chalkboard. Exams are hard, but not impossible w/very steep curve. Help-sessions are very helpful and I highly advise to attend.  Dr. Johnson is one of the kindest professors at UNC and really cares about his students.  He should win a Nobel Prize in Chemistry! (Take him and you'll get the joke)

You have your group to work with, and if you study, you'll do great!

Professor Sevetson has a very flexible way of administering exams, giving projects and exams for every unit. As long as you don't procrastinate and truly engage with the topic, this course will be an easy A. She curves exams based on how the class did. She makes an effort to get to know you and wants to see you succeed.

Dr. Sevetson is the best professor I have ever had! Her lectures are hilarious, and she knows how to "dumb down" hard topics for you to understand. She gives out a lot of group projects and group assessments, so choose your group wisely. I would 100% take this class again.

Takes class WAY too seriously. Can never "game" attendance because she makes sure to count people in classroom and compare it with PollEv numbers. review_highlights.comment: Very difficult. Lecture is not useful. Just read the powerpoint/PDF but seldom write down on blackboard, so it is hard to understand his ideas. Exams are difficult, don't expect to learn much from him. Self-learn actually is much better.

I think the class's greatest flaw is the sheer number of hours you must invest in OH. The assignments are not designed for you to solve on your own. For those of you that must take it: find a good study group (I owe my grade to this; saves you from burnout). Do your best on assignments/readings/quizzes. Worship the TAs. Try your best on the tests.

I personally really enjoyed this class. Yes, it's hard- it's true that you will spend a lot of time in OH, but I honestly think people over-exaggerate how bad it is. If you put in the effort throughout the class, you shouldn't find yourself cramming for the exams. Jack is also extremely generous with grading. Take it if you're math/logic savvy

If you have to take this class, don't do it during a hard semester (looking at you 17-credit hour folks), this class demands a LOT of time and it's not worth risking your GPA. It's a nice balance to a lighter slate of classes. Them Disney lessons about teamwork makes the dreamwork are true while you're here. Your CS students, you got this!

This class is like if Jack was your swim instruction when you were 3 and he asks what you know about swimming. You say well I know you move your arms and legs. He says "Great" then pushes you in the water. Right before you drown he picks you up and says, "Now what did you do wrong?" after you give a answer he pushes you in again. Rinse and Repeat.

review_highlights.comment: People are hating on Dr. Nowlan, but she's the best. Don't be a lazy bum and you'll be fine. Exams are easy.

Dr. Nowlan is really nice and caring, and she's very open to talking about the intersection of neuroscience and humanities. I learned a lot from this class but she would run out of time in pretty much every lecture. Don't need to read the textbook, all exam questions come from the lectures. Hated the CREATE method project though, very boring.

Dr. Nowlan is an amazing professor. Her lectures are primarily open-discussion, so it is important to come to class to participate. She gives many extra credit opportunities. She heavily uses Gradescope and gives a one-day grace period for a lot of her assignments. It is important to stay ahead on deadlines and give max effort on assignments.

Dr. Nowlan is very supportive and there are a lot of built-in drops and extra credit. Exams test comprehension on pretty complex research papers, so take time to understand them well a few days before. The Makerspace project is a lot, but by the end you become super informed on a specific drug and receptor. We had a cool field trip as well.

I liked Dr Nowlan in 221 so I wanted to take 405 with her but this class isn't what I expected it to be. She is super sweet but the class itself isn't fun and I feel like I haven't learned that much about neuropharmacology but more just about research papers. Feels difficult balancing the semester long project in between all the paper assignments.

She is such an amazing and caring professor! The tests are very straightforward and from the lectures and she gives study guides. I loved her the sweetest.

This is a review for COMP 581 - Intro to Robotics
Great class with hands-on group projects where you build your lego robot and program it to complete tasks. The material covered in the lectures and exams is relevant to help you build your robot.

My only complaint is that sometimes the lectures move slowly covering basic introductions for too long.

Why are there negative reviews? Because there were no quizes or exams, and no one studied regularly. When professor asked students questions, no one answered because they did not study. Because of this, Professor would never offer a course again where there is no quiz or exams. And its the students fault.

Human Robot Interaction course. A research based course. Awesome Professor, good as a Kris Jordan. No midterms, quizes or exams. Projects, discussions, papers and presentations. If you are interested in an intro to research course and research related to Robotics, this course is for you.

review_highlights.comment:
POLI 75 is a great course for anybody mildly interested in law, and Prof Szypszak is an incredible lecturer. Make sure you read before class, he cold calls and docks your participation if you can't demonstrate a basic understanding of the reading. 

One of those classes where it's more important to show that you're trying than it is to be correct.

Awesome professor! If you are interested in pre-law this class is a MUST. This course is mostly reading cases and lectures, a legal research exercise, a paper, and two exams. His lectures are highly engaging as he really understands the material and brings in anecdotes. Introduces the different fields of law and what being a lawyer is actually like

Professor Szypszak is a fantastic lecturer and professor. He seems scary at first but he is super approachable if you want to talk to him after class. Just do the readings and pay attention in class and you will be fine!

Favorite class I've taken at Carolina. Szypszak is an amazing person and such a good lecturer (he even made property law interesting and not boring). The class itself isn't difficult either. Do the readings and participate in discussion and you'll do fine, but reading is definitely important. I just wish he taught more undergrad classes.

This class is definitely more difficult than most of FYS, but Prof. Szypszak is a nice man who talks a lot about his experiences. This class exposes you to different fields of law, which is helpful for Pre-Law students. Grading is fair and you will end up knowing so much more about American law and what lawyers do after this class.

review_highlights.comment: Dr. T and Sports Xtra are great. It's definitely a difficult class, but you get out what you put in. Since the class is a student-run broadcast, you mostly learn from other students, but T is always there for guidance, support, and critiques when needed. 129 and 523 are the best opportunities but don't take unless you are serious about broadcast.

Dr. T expects a lot in Sports Xtra, and the main benefits of the class are to gain practical experience covering literally every UNC sporting event and to develop truly great friendships with people in the class. He doesn't teach much at all, rather leaving students to learn from each other, but offers accurate constructive criticism instead.

Dr. T actively made my life worse during the time I spent with him. Nothing I learned in Sports Xtra was thanks to him. We, as students, taught him more about the things we were using than he taught us. Sports Xtra on its own is great, but I would never recommend any student take a class headed by T. The j school will be better when he retires.

Been awhile since T got a review. I. LOVE. T. He's always willing to go out of his way to help his students. He's tough, but he's personable. I took Sports Xtra, which he supervised since it's a student-run broadcast. He wants his students to succeed and is by far one of my favorite people at UNC. If you are interested in broadcast, he's your guy.

Sports Xtra is a part-time job if you want an A or B. It looks good on a resume and when networking but seems higher stress than it's worth. Students run everything and T pops in for critiques, so the peer hierarchy plays a large role in your success and access to opportunities. Brace yourself for a lot of last-minute scrambling if you take it.

Professor Tucker is incredibly patient and caring. She grades based on improvement, not just achievement, which I appreciated immensely. The workshop set up of the class itself is a little tricky if you're not used to sharing your work with others, but Dr. Tucker does a great job facilitating positive feedback. Highly recommend for an FC-CREATE.

The best prof I've had at UNC. She was so understanding regarding everything-if you were sick, going through something, etc. She's a phenomenal person and professor- very helpful with perfecting your writing regardless of what your writing level was. Nice but super liberal. Got a 100 on everything. Be ready to have your short stories read and discussed. Participation is important. Super chill class. Doesn't like when you miss class. Dr. Tucker is the best! She truly cares about her students and wants them to become better writers. I have never felt so cared for by a teacher. Lectures were boring but not super important to pay attention to. Gave us time to complete our discussion boards in class. No final exam, just a big group project but he gives plenty of time to work on it.

professor Steelman was easy to understand, his classes were a mix of lecture, practice in R, and group work. None of the assignments were too difficult or time consuming. The biggest grade in the class comes from a big group project that you work on during the second half of the semester.

Professor Steelman is a very laid back professor that makes getting an A very attainable and easy. 50% of the grade is a semester-long group polling project and 40% is attendance, so just show up to class and put in work and you'll get an A. Additionally, the information that we learn in class has been extremely informative. I highly recommend this class if you are someone who enjoys learning. Professor Ziad is a hidden gem.

There is a reading once a week with an easy discussion post to go along with it. The only other grades are the final (3 essays that he gave us the prompts for ahead of time) and a group presentation. The class is interesting and mostly discussion based in and out of class.

Waleed is a master of Islamic studies. He's gonna throw a lot of information at you, but when he tells you to get the full picture, listen to him. Know a couple of examples well, and go to recitation, and you'll be fine.

Midterm/final open-book, but they still set it up so you need to study

If you do the readings and not wait until the last minute to write the 10 page paper (like I did) then you will most likely get an A in the class.

Brigitte is intimidating at first but she's kind overall and passionate about this class. The key here is to be on good terms with your TA. Dr. Zimmerman was a little dry, but she def. knew her stuff. I was worried at the beginning because she goes pretty fast, but I got used to it. There's a big paper due that is 25% of your grade, and she gives 3 random pop quizzes (drops the lowest). Not a terrible class, but I didn't like PLCY.
